answer: Each identity deposits one distinct heirloom seed accession in a cedar vault box, its DNA fingerprint hashed at intake. Quarterly, verifiers germinate a random 20-seed sample and re-sequence seedlings; below 70% germination or a matched fingerprint revokes the slot and burns a 5-coin bond. After a gale or tide flood, staff recheck box seals within 48 hours. One accession yields one identity, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 provenanced lots, $95 yearly storage each and years of breeding to create new distinct lines; trade-off: rare varieties are scarce, so admission is slow.
